title: Filter Bank CSP with Riemannian Weighting for Motor Imagery BCI
author: Souissi Jihen

steps.title: Prepare Python environment
steps.instruction: Install and import Python 3.6 together with the libraries MNE, NumPy, scikit‑learn and SciPy.

steps.title: Load EEG dataset
steps.instruction: Read the BCI Competition IV dataset 2a files (extension .gdf) into an MNE Raw object (e.g., raw_data = mne.io.read_raw_gdf('subjectX.gdf')).

steps.title: Create epochs from raw data
steps.instruction: Segment the continuous EEG into epochs synchronized to stimulus events using the event dictionary (event_id=stims) and the following parameters: tmin = ‑0.5 s, tmax = 1.5 s, baseline = (‑0.2 s, 0 s), preload=True.

substeps.instruction: epochs = mne.Epochs(raw_data, events, event_id=stims, tmin=-0.5, tmax=1.5, baseline=(-0.2, 0), preload=True)

steps.title: Apply band‑pass FIR filter
steps.instruction: Filter each epoch with a FIR Butterworth band‑pass filter (frequency limits as defined in the study; implementation uses MNE’s filtering functions).

steps.title: Extract weighted CSP features
steps.instruction: Pass the filtered epochs to the custom function RW‑FBCSP (Riemannian‑Weighting Filter Bank Common Spatial Pattern) which implements CSP with an OVR scheme in a Riemannian space and returns a reduced, informative feature vector for each trial.

steps.title: Assemble feature matrix and labels
steps.instruction: Collect the feature vectors produced by RW‑FBCSP for each subject together with their corresponding class labels into X (features) and y (labels).

steps.title: Partition data for training and validation
steps.instruction: For each subject, split X and y into a test set (held‑out for final evaluation) and a training set; within the training set further divide 80 % for classifier training and 20 % for hyper‑parameter validation using 5‑fold cross‑validation (KFold).

steps.title: Evaluate classifiers and record metrics
steps.instruction: For each subject and each classifier, predict the labels of the held‑out test set, then compute Accuracy, Precision, Recall and F1‑score; store the values in global lists and later average them across the nine subjects.

steps.title: Combine predictions with majority voting
steps.instruction: Create a voting‑classifier pipeline that takes the three individual predictions (LDA, RFC, MLP) and outputs the majority‑vote decision; display a preview of the merged predictions.

steps.title: Generate summary tables
steps.instruction: Use pandas.DataFrame to build summary tables that list the performance metrics for each classifier and for the voting ensemble (e.g., test results obtained by RFC).
